summary:
The two label-to-figure statistics cannot discriminate yet, and the reason is not the annotations. Both were run on the manuscript and on a one-table reuse chain's text laid onto the same pages (my scribe, PR #620, cut 'book', so the label lines of every page are filled from the chain like the running text): label_in_page_text and feature_label_share return not-a-number on the evaluation pages, on the training pages, on the whole book, for the manuscript and for the chain alike. Neither passes, neither fails; the check has no discriminating power today.

WHY. vs/dsl.py pictures() reads only picture items whose verdict is AGREED, and that verdict is computed at read time: a folio's annotation is AGREED once a second, independent seat has annotated the same folio and the two agree on kind and on at least 80 per cent of the features both recorded. Of the 50 picture items on the record exactly one folio reaches AGREED, f72v1, and its 32 objects carry no label field at all; the joined-label inference for that circular page matches none of them to a label line. _picture_objects is therefore empty and both statistics return not-a-number.

WHAT IS ALREADY THERE. Across those same 50 draft annotations there are 1,395 objects; 683 carry a label field and 682 of those name a label line that exists in the text (the book holds 892 label lines), spread over 14 folios: f99r 98 label-linked objects, f73r and f73v 64 each, f70v2 61, f72v1, f72v2 and f72v3 60 each, f68r1 58, and more. The linkage the statistics need exists in the drafts and is far above min_objects 10. What is missing is the agreement rule, not the data. This is what M-L4 reported from its side in PR #448, 'picture annotations cannot reach AGREED as scored', which was closed unmerged, as was PR #431 which landed the statistics' tests.

WHAT WOULD UNBLOCK IT. One second, independent annotation of any one of those 14 folios by a different seat, or matching objects by label locus in the agreement rule instead of by kind and order. Either makes at least one label-linked folio AGREED, both statistics become computable on the hidden pages with objects to spare, and the control asked for in (2) can be run for real: a chain has no access to the drawings, so it should fail label_in_page_text where the manuscript passes, and until that asymmetry is demonstrated the step's own rule stands - no further invented language is worth designing, and none of the ones filed (R-035, 11/22, invented_language) predicts a label fact because none was registrable.

REGISTERED. fact.json holds label_in_page_text with its threshold fixed before looking (the label-dealt null, p at most 0.01, 199 deals, min_objects 10). The second registration this step asks for is the same compare against feature_label_share:
{"statistic": {"picture_label": {"test": "feature_label_share", "min_objects": 10}}, "compare": [{"null": "shuffle_picture_labels", "direction": "greater", "p": 0.01, "perms": 199}]}

Both are filed so that they can be scored the day an AGREED label-linked folio exists; filing them now also fixes the thresholds before anyone sees a value.
